preceding_messages.text: I adopt the 2 mm dowel-pin datum, the degraded monthly transect re-measurement, the 1 mm drift threshold, and the "DATUM ABSENT — INTEGRITY UNRESOLVED — CONSERVATIVE SPAN APPLIED" annotation verbatim; they give the peg-integrity question a defined degraded-mode exit rather than an indefinite weekly check against a missing datum. The gap your monthly cadence leaves open is sustained external obstruction: a four-month municipal road-rebuild project fences off the structure, no transect can be completed within any single month, the conservative span persists indefinitely, and queued inter-site audit triggers accumulate without resolution. I therefore mandate that if the monthly transect is obstructed for more than one consecutive month, the peg is retired under the full relocation-review protocol at the first scheduled access window, and any queued trigger older than the new-site's first monthly NIST cross-check is retired under a bold "OBSOLETE — ACCESS UNRESOLVED" annotation rather than executed upon eventual access, so the audit trail records that the trigger was retired by structural inaccessibility rather than abandoned. The concrete failure this closes: the construction fence comes down in month five, the delayed transect confirms the peg drifted 0.8 mm (within the 1 mm tolerance), the conservative span lifts, and the queued week-6 pressure-spread trigger—originally raised by a temporary construction crane that departed in week 14—executes an immediate elevation-recording audit against a coordinate where no transient remains, dispatching a crew to verify a vanished artifact and printing an appendix entry a year-two resident reads as institutional confusion rather than statistical conservatism.

preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the peg-retirement-on-sustained-obstruction rule and the "OBSOLETE — ACCESS UNRESOLVED" retirement annotation verbatim; they give the indefinite conservative span a defined structural exit without requiring access that may never come. Because your age-based retirement criterion leaves open triggers raised *during* the obstruction period whose physical context has vanished by the time access resumes, I mandate that every queued inter-site trigger carry a three-field context tag—obstruction type, estimated departure condition, and the week-number at which the transient was last physically confirmed present at the site—logged by the original observer at the moment of queuing. The failure this closes: during month two of the fence period a weekly construction-equipment delivery truck parked at Site 3's northern edge trips the 0.5 hPa inter-site spread, the trigger is queued with the truck present, but by month five when access resumes the delivery schedule has ended and the trigger—being younger than the new-site's first NIST cross-check—executes an immediate elevation-recording audit against a coordinate where no truck, no crane, and no transient of any kind remains, dispatching a crew to verify a vanished artifact and printing an appendix entry a year-two resident reads as procedural incoherence. I therefore require that upon access resumption the compiler cross-references each queued trigger's context tag against the current horizon-sketch photograph; if the tagged obstruction is absent from that photograph the trigger is retired under the same "OBSOLETE — ACCESS UNRESOLVED" annotation with the added tag "CONTEXT LAPSAT ACCESS" rather than executed, so the audit trail records that the transient departed before the crew could reach the site rather than that the crew was sent and found nothing.

target.text: I adopt the three-field context tag, the access-resumption cross-reference, and the "CONTEXT LAPSED AT ACCESS" retirement annotation verbatim; they close the vanished-transient dispatch hole by making the audit trail record the obstruction's departure rather than the crew's futile arrival. Because a single-photograph present/absent test has the temporal resolution of one instant, I mandate that the access-resumption observer update the context tag's departure-estimate field with a current on-site assessment and that any trigger whose updated estimate places departure within 48 hours of the scheduled crew-arrival window is held under a bold "CONTEXT TRANSIENT — DEPARTURE IMMINENT" annotation pending a second confirmation photograph taken no more than six hours before dispatch. The concrete failure this closes: during month-five's access-resumption photograph a recurring weekly delivery truck sits at Site 3's northern edge, the context tag matches, and the trigger executes an immediate elevation-recording audit dispatched for 14:00; the truck completes its delivery at 11:00 and departs, so the crew arrives to find no transient, the apparatus already vacated, and an appendix entry that reads as a verification failure rather than a context lapse.
